summary: Full backend + frontend testing of SolopreneurWriter completed. 14/14 pytest backend tests passed (auth, articles CRUD, prompts, filtering, ownership isolation). 20/20 frontend Playwright checks passed covering login, register, logout, dashboard filters, article workspace split panels, title sync, tags, status dropdown, reference links, word count, save, prompt drawer (open/copy/edit/save), back navigation, and empty state for new users.
critical_code_review_comments: ArticleWorkspacePage auto-save useEffect (line 70-75) depends only on [article] but calls saveArticle which is recreated whenever title/notes/tags change. The interval captures the initial saveArticle closure on mount, so auto-save every 30s may persist stale state. Recommend including saveArticle in the dependency array or using a ref to always call the latest version. (Low priority — manual Save works correctly.)
Backend sets cookies with secure=False. Acceptable for dev, but in production deployment behind HTTPS this should be True (recommend env-based toggle).
Login endpoint updates locked_until on every failed attempt, which effectively resets the 15-minute lockout window each try. This is stricter than typical lockout semantics — confirm intentional.
server.py is 420 lines but still a single file covering auth/articles/prompts/storage. Consider splitting into routers if feature set grows (>700 line rule not yet hit).
test_credentials: admin@example.com / admin123 (confirmed working; also registered uitest_* ephemeral user)
seed_data_creation: Created one article titled 'My UI Test Article' in admin account via UI flow (status=draft, tags=ui-test,playwright, 1 reference link). Tests clean up their own TEST_-prefixed artifacts via pytest fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py and are idempotent (self-cleanup). Admin login credentials are admin@example.com/admin123. The app uses httpOnly cookies so requests.Session() is required (no Authorization header needed). Auto-save fires every 30s; only flag as a bug if UX issue observed.
